intents: so small that it makes no real difference and you can safely ignore it
when a price goes up by one penny and nobody would even notice
describing a risk, effect or cost too tiny to worry about
ru_cue: настолько мало, что можно не принимать в расчет

upgrades.plain: Don't panic about the scratch, the damage is [so small it doesn't matter].
upgrades.better: Don't panic about the scratch, the damage is *negligible*.

upgrades.plain: I switched banks to save money, and the savings turned out to be [almost nothing]. I felt so silly.
upgrades.better: I switched banks to save money, and the savings turned out to be *negligible*. I felt so silly.

upgrades.plain: The risk is [really tiny] if you follow the instructions.
upgrades.better: The risk is *negligible* if you follow the instructions.

nuance: Stronger than 'small': small enough to ignore completely. The opposite of substantial.
personal: What is one habit of yours whose effect on your health is probably negligible?
Who do you know who worries about risks that are negligible?
gesture: Pinch your thumb and finger until they almost touch, then flick the tiny thing away.
hook: Sounds like 'neglect-able': so small you can simply neglect it.

intents: large enough in amount or size to really matter
when the discount is nearly half the price, not just a few pounds
describing a big sum of money, a big rise in prices or a filling meal
ru_cue: немалый по размеру или количеству, ощутимый

upgrades.plain: They offered me a [big] pay rise, so I'm staying.
upgrades.better: They offered me a *substantial* pay rise, so I'm staying.

upgrades.plain: The house needs [a lot of] work before we can move in, and the baby is due in May.
upgrades.better: The house needs *substantial* work before we can move in, and the baby is due in May.

upgrades.plain: The bank wants a [large] deposit before they'll give us the mortgage.
upgrades.better: The bank wants a *substantial* deposit before they'll give us the mortgage.

ru_trap: Russian 'существенный' often means 'important'; English substantial is mainly about size or amount (a substantial sum, not a substantial remark).
nuance: Mainly about amount or size; for a deep emotional or intellectual effect, profound fits better.
personal: What was the last substantial purchase you made, and was it worth it?
Who in your family has made a substantial change to their life recently?
hook: Think 'substance': something with real weight in your hands, a big solid portion.

intents: describing a plan or business that could actually work and survive in real life, not just on paper
when you check whether a plan is possible with the money and time you really have
an option you could really go with, because it would succeed in practice
ru_cue: такой, что действительно может сработать на практике

upgrades.plain: Cycling to work isn't [a realistic option] if there's nowhere safe to leave the bike.
upgrades.better: Cycling to work isn't a *viable* option if there's nowhere safe to leave the bike.

upgrades.plain: We put all our savings into the café idea, but on that budget it was never [going to work].
upgrades.better: We put all our savings into the café idea, but on that budget it was never *viable*.

upgrades.plain: We need a [workable] alternative to the ferry.
upgrades.better: We need a *viable* alternative to the ferry.

nuance: Asks 'will it work in practice?'; plausible asks 'does it sound true?', sustainable asks 'can it last?'
personal: Is working from home a viable option in your job or studies?
Which friend of yours has a business idea that might actually be viable?
hook: Latin 'vita' (life), as in 'vital': a viable plan has a heartbeat, it can live in the real world.

intents: skip steps to save time or money, so the work ends up done badly
when builders use cheap materials to finish early and the roof leaks a year later
do a job the quick, careless way instead of doing it properly
ru_cue: экономить время или деньги в ущерб качеству

upgrades.plain: The builders [did a cheap, rushed job] on the roof, and it leaked within a year.
upgrades.better: The builders *cut corners* on the roof, and it leaked within a year.

upgrades.plain: I [rushed through the boring parts] of my dissertation, and my supervisor spotted it straight away. So embarrassing.
upgrades.better: I *cut corners* on my dissertation, and my supervisor spotted it straight away. So embarrassing.

upgrades.plain: Never [skip steps] when you're wiring a house.
upgrades.better: Never *cut corners* when you're wiring a house.

ru_trap: Russian 'срезать угол' is a literal shortcut on foot; English cut corners always means doing a job badly to save time or money.
nuance: Always negative: quality is lost. Making a process simpler without losing quality is streamline.
personal: When did you cut corners on something and regret it later?
Who do you know who never cuts corners, even on tiny jobs?
gesture: Slice your hand diagonally across the corner of the table, as if trimming it off.
hook: Picture a builder snipping the corners off every brick to finish faster, and the wall starting to wobble.

intents: able to keep going for years without running out of energy, money or resources
a pace or habit you could keep up for a long time without burning out
farming or fishing that doesn't use up nature faster than it can recover
ru_cue: такой, что может продолжаться долго, не истощая силы и ресурсы

upgrades.plain: Working seventy hours a week just isn't [something you can keep up]; my wife barely sees me.
upgrades.better: Working seventy hours a week just isn't *sustainable*; my wife barely sees me.

upgrades.plain: The farm uses [eco-friendly] methods that keep the soil healthy.
upgrades.better: The farm uses *sustainable* methods that keep the soil healthy.

upgrades.plain: The charity needs an income [that will last], not one big gift.
upgrades.better: The charity needs a *sustainable* income, not one big gift.

collocations.chunk: not sustainable in the long term

ru_trap: Russian 'устойчивое развитие' tempts 'stable development'; English says sustainable development.
nuance: About lasting without using things up; viable is only about whether something works at all.
personal: Honestly, is your current sleep schedule sustainable?
Who do you know who has found a sustainable way to stay fit?
hook: Like the sustain pedal on a piano: it keeps the note going and going without fading.

intents: dealing with problems in a practical, realistic way rather than chasing the ideal
describing someone sensible who fixes what they can afford now and leaves the rest for next year
describing someone who asks 'what actually works?' instead of 'what's perfect?'
ru_cue: решающий задачи практично, без идеализма

upgrades.plain: Let's be [practical]: we can't afford a new kitchen, so we'll just paint it.
upgrades.better: Let's be *pragmatic*: we can't afford a new kitchen, so we'll just paint it.

upgrades.plain: Mum wanted the perfect wedding, but Dad took a [realistic] view and booked the village hall.
upgrades.better: Mum wanted the perfect wedding, but Dad took a *pragmatic* view and booked the village hall.

upgrades.plain: Her advice was [practical] rather than comforting.
upgrades.better: Her advice was *pragmatic* rather than comforting.

nuance: Usually a compliment in English (sensible, realistic), not 'cold and calculating'; the opposite is idealistic.
personal: In which part of your life are you most pragmatic?
Who is the most pragmatic person in your family?
hook: Same root as Russian 'прагматик': the person who asks 'does it work?', not 'is it beautiful?'

intents: so convincing that you can't really argue against it
when the evidence is so strong that the jury agrees in ten minutes
a story so gripping that you have to know what happens next
describing a reason so strong and convincing that you feel you have to act on it
ru_cue: настолько убедительный или захватывающий, что невозможно отмахнуться

upgrades.plain: She made a [really convincing] case for the extra funding, and the boss said yes on the spot.
upgrades.better: She made a *compelling* case for the extra funding, and the boss said yes on the spot.

upgrades.plain: I can't see any [good] reason to move house.
upgrades.better: I can't see any *compelling* reason to move house.

upgrades.plain: The plot was so [gripping that I had to know what happened next] that I watched it all in one night and was a wreck at work the next day.
upgrades.better: The plot was so *compelling* that I watched it all in one night and was a wreck at work the next day.

nuance: Stronger than plausible: plausible only sounds possible, compelling makes you believe it or keep watching.
personal: What is the most compelling book or series you've ever finished in one go?
Who do you know who can make a compelling case for almost anything?
hook: Sounds like 'kom-PELmeni': a plate of пельмени so good you can't stop until it's empty.

intents: sounds believable and could be true, though you can't be sure
when someone's excuse sounds reasonable until you check the dates
an explanation that makes enough sense to accept for now
ru_cue: похоже на правду, хотя не доказано

upgrades.plain: His excuse sounded [believable] until we checked the dates.
upgrades.better: His excuse sounded *plausible* until we checked the dates.

upgrades.plain: In the interview I struggled to give a [believable] reason for leaving my last job.
upgrades.better: In the interview I struggled to give a *plausible* reason for leaving my last job.

upgrades.plain: That's a [reasonable] explanation for the noise.
upgrades.better: That's a *plausible* explanation for the noise.

nuance: Only says something sounds true, often with a hint of doubt; compelling means it actually convinces you.
personal: What is the most plausible excuse you've ever used to get out of something?
Who do you know who can make any story sound plausible?
hook: Think 'applause-ible': a story good enough to get applause, even if it's made up.

intents: finally make yourself do the unpleasant thing you've been putting off
when you stop delaying and book the dentist, even though you dread it
accept the pain of a hard decision because there's no way around it
ru_cue: собраться с духом и сделать неприятное, но неизбежное дело

upgrades.plain: I finally [made myself call] the dentist after three weeks of toothache.
upgrades.better: I finally *bit the bullet* and called the dentist after three weeks of toothache.

upgrades.plain: We'll have to [accept the cost] and buy a new boiler before winter.
upgrades.better: We'll have to *bite the bullet* and buy a new boiler before winter.

upgrades.plain: I [forced myself] to tell my parents I was dropping out, and my hands were shaking.
upgrades.better: I *bit the bullet* and told my parents I was dropping out, and my hands were shaking.

collocations.chunk: had to bite the bullet and pay

nuance: About forcing yourself through something unpleasant you've been avoiding, not about doing extra (go the extra mile).
personal: What is something you need to bite the bullet and do this month?
When did someone you know bite the bullet and make a big change?
gesture: Clench your teeth, squeeze your eyes shut, then give one firm nod: go.
hook: Picture a soldier biting on a bullet while the doctor works: it hurts, but he gets it over with.

intents: could be understood in more than one way, so you're not sure what's meant
when her reply 'maybe, we'll see' leaves you not knowing if she's coming
wording that two people can read and come away with different meanings
ru_cue: можно понять по-разному, и неясно, что имелось в виду

upgrades.plain: The instructions were [unclear], so half the class did the wrong task.
upgrades.better: The instructions were *ambiguous*, so half the class did the wrong task.

upgrades.plain: He texted 'we need to talk', which was so [unclear] that I didn't sleep all night.
upgrades.better: He texted 'we need to talk', which was so *ambiguous* that I didn't sleep all night.

upgrades.plain: The contract was [vague] about who pays for repairs.
upgrades.better: The contract was *ambiguous* about who pays for repairs.

ru_trap: Don't mix it up with ambitious (амбициозный); ambiguous means двусмысленный.
nuance: About words or signals with more than one possible meaning; a situation where the rules are unclear is a grey area.
personal: When did an ambiguous message from someone make you worry for nothing?
Who do you know who gives ambiguous answers when they don't want to commit?
hook: 'Ambi' means both, as in ambidextrous: words that point both ways at once, like a sign with two arrows.

intents: far too big (or too small) compared with what it should match
when a teenager is grounded for a month for coming home ten minutes late
taking up an oversized, unfair share of the money, time or work
ru_cue: слишком большой по сравнению с тем, чему должен соответствовать
plain: way bigger than it should be

upgrades.plain: Being grounded for a month for one late night felt [way over the top].
upgrades.better: Being grounded for a month for one late night felt *disproportionate*.

upgrades.plain: Rent takes [a huge, unfair] share of my salary.
upgrades.better: Rent takes a *disproportionate* share of my salary.

upgrades.plain: She does [far more than her fair share] of the housework, and she's had enough.
upgrades.better: She does a *disproportionate* amount of the housework, and she's had enough.

ru_trap: Russian 'несоразмерный с...' tempts 'with'; English says disproportionate to something.
nuance: One thing out of scale with another; a gap between groups (rich and poor) is a disparity.
personal: When did you have a disproportionate reaction to something small?
Who do you know who spends a disproportionate amount of money on one hobby?
hook: Picture a tiny head on a giant body: everything out of proportion.

intents: so different from each other that they seem to have nothing in common
when a team is a farmer, a lawyer and a DJ who somehow have to work together
a random mix of unrelated things that don't fit into one picture
ru_cue: совершенно разные, ничем не связанные между собой

upgrades.plain: The committee brought together [very different] groups who rarely agree.
upgrades.better: The committee brought together *disparate* groups who rarely agree.

upgrades.plain: Her interests are [all over the place], from welding to ballet.
upgrades.better: Her interests are wildly *disparate*, from welding to ballet.

upgrades.plain: At our wedding, our two [completely different] families had to share one table, and I was terrified.
upgrades.better: At our wedding, our two *disparate* families had to share one table, and I was terrified.

nuance: Describes things that are unlike each other; disparity is an unfair gap between groups (pay, wealth).
personal: Which two disparate interests of yours would surprise people?
Who do you know whose friends come from totally disparate backgrounds?
hook: 'dis-PAR-ate' sounds like 'не пара' (not a pair): these things are no match for each other at all.

intents: has never happened before, with nothing like it in the past to compare
when even the oldest people in the village can't remember a summer this hot
a record level of something that breaks with all of history
ru_cue: такого раньше никогда не случалось

upgrades.plain: The heat this summer was [like nothing anyone had seen before].
upgrades.better: The heat this summer was *unprecedented*.

upgrades.plain: After the advert, demand reached [record] levels and we sold out in a day.
upgrades.better: After the advert, demand reached *unprecedented* levels and we sold out in a day.

upgrades.plain: She won by a [never-before-seen] margin, and her coach was in tears.
upgrades.better: She won by an *unprecedented* margin, and her coach was in tears.

nuance: Means there is no earlier example at all; something merely sudden or unexpected is out of the blue.
personal: What was an unprecedented moment in your own life, a first of its kind?
Who do you know who achieved something unprecedented in their family?
hook: Think 'un-PRESIDENT-ed': something so new that no president before ever had to deal with it.

intents: strong and solid enough to take rough treatment without breaking
boots that can survive years of hiking through mud and rocks
an argument, system or evidence that stands up to tough testing and criticism
ru_cue: крепкий, выдерживает нагрузки и критику

upgrades.plain: These boots are [really strong] and will last for years.
upgrades.better: These boots are *robust* and will last for years.

upgrades.plain: The examiner tore into my thesis, but my argument was [strong enough] to survive it.
upgrades.better: The examiner tore into my thesis, but my argument was *robust* enough to survive it.

upgrades.plain: My grandmother is in [really good] health at ninety.
upgrades.better: My grandmother is in *robust* health at ninety.

nuance: Stresses not breaking under pressure; resilience is about bouncing back after something has gone wrong.
personal: What is the most robust thing you own, something that has survived everything?
Who do you know who is in robust health despite their age?
gesture: Bang your fist firmly on the table, then flex your arm: solid.
hook: 'RO-bust' sounds like 'robot bust': a solid metal robot statue you can drop without a scratch.

intents: start to be able to do something after a few clumsy tries
when the new software finally clicks after a week of fumbling
pick up how a skill works through practice, so it stops feeling awkward
ru_cue: после нескольких попыток начать справляться с чем-то

upgrades.plain: Driving felt impossible at first, but I [learned how to do it] in a month.
upgrades.better: Driving felt impossible at first, but I *got the hang of* it in a month.

upgrades.plain: Don't worry, you'll [figure the machine out] by Friday.
upgrades.better: Don't worry, you'll *get the hang of* the machine by Friday.

upgrades.plain: I nearly cried over my first three loaves, but now I've finally [learned how to make] bread.
upgrades.better: I nearly cried over my first three loaves, but now I've finally *got the hang of* making bread.

collocations.chunk: once you get the hang of it
never quite got the hang of
starting to get the hang of it

nuance: The moment a skill starts to work for you; once it is fully automatic it has become second nature.
personal: What is something you got the hang of recently that once felt impossible?
Who taught you something patiently until you got the hang of it?
hook: Picture hanging a picture: crooked five times, then on the sixth try you get the hang of it.

intents: very deep and serious, reaching right into how someone thinks or lives
describing an effect that goes very deep, like losing a parent changing how someone sees everything
describing a very deep feeling, a heavy silence or a deep knowledge of a subject
ru_cue: настолько глубокий, что меняет человека или его жизнь

upgrades.plain: Losing his dad had a [really deep] effect on the way he lives.
upgrades.better: Losing his dad had a *profound* effect on the way he lives.

upgrades.plain: There was a [deep] silence after she read the letter out.
upgrades.better: There was a *profound* silence after she read the letter out.

upgrades.plain: My grandmother has a [deep] knowledge of plants: she can name every weed in the garden.
upgrades.better: My grandmother has a *profound* knowledge of plants: she can name every weed in the garden.

nuance: About depth, emotional or intellectual; for a large amount or size use substantial.
personal: Which book or film had a profound effect on you?
Who has had the most profound influence on your life?
hook: 'pro-FOUND': found at the very bottom of the deepest ocean.

intents: certain to happen sooner or later, whatever anyone does
when you have three small kids, so a messy house is bound to happen no matter how hard you try
the result everyone could see coming, with no way to avoid it
ru_cue: то, что обязательно случится, как ни старайся

upgrades.plain: With three kids in the house, a bit of mess is [bound to happen].
upgrades.better: With three kids in the house, a bit of mess is *inevitable*.

upgrades.plain: After all those delays, missing the deadline was [unavoidable], but I still dreaded telling the client.
upgrades.better: After all those delays, missing the deadline was *inevitable*, but I still dreaded telling the client.

upgrades.plain: It's [certain] that prices will go up again.
upgrades.better: It's *inevitable* that prices will go up again.

nuance: About one outcome that can't be avoided; something that happens every single time happens invariably.
personal: What is one inevitable part of your week that you'd love to skip?
Who do you know who is always late, so that waiting for them is inevitable?
hook: 'in-EVIT-able' sounds like 'can't-evict-able': you can't evict it, it moves in no matter what.

intents: full of tiny details and parts that all link together
describing lace, a carving or a watch's gears that took hours of fine work
a plot or pattern so detailed that you need a second look to follow it
ru_cue: из множества мелких деталей, сложно переплетенных между собой

upgrades.plain: The cake was covered in [really detailed] patterns that must have taken hours.
upgrades.better: The cake was covered in *intricate* patterns that must have taken hours.

upgrades.plain: The plot is [really complicated], so I had to read it twice.
upgrades.better: The plot is *intricate*, so I had to read it twice.

upgrades.plain: My grandfather spent a whole winter on that [detailed] model ship, and the cat knocked it over in a second.
upgrades.better: My grandfather spent a whole winter on that *intricate* model ship, and the cat knocked it over in a second.

ru_trap: Sounds like 'интрига' or intriguing, but intricate means detailed and complex, not interesting.
nuance: Describes the thing (many fine connected parts); the careful person who makes it is meticulous.
personal: What is the most intricate thing you've ever made or repaired?
Who do you know who loves intricate work, like knitting, models or puzzles?
gesture: With your fingertips, weave tiny loops in the air, as if threading fine lace.
hook: 'in-TRICK-ate': a magician's trick box packed with tiny hidden gears and springs.

intents: only the most basic level, with nothing more advanced added
when you can order food in a language and that's about it
simple and undeveloped, like a first version or a shelter with only the bare essentials
ru_cue: самый начальный уровень, только азы

upgrades.plain: My Spanish is [pretty basic]: I can order food and not much else.
upgrades.better: My Spanish is *rudimentary*: I can order food and not much else.

upgrades.plain: The cabin only had [very basic] plumbing, and my sister refused to stay.
upgrades.better: The cabin only had *rudimentary* plumbing, and my sister refused to stay.

upgrades.plain: My [basic] first aid was enough until the ambulance arrived, and I've never been so relieved.
upgrades.better: My *rudimentary* first aid was enough until the ambulance arrived, and I've never been so relieved.

ru_trap: False friend: Russian 'рудиментарный' means a useless leftover; English rudimentary means basic, at beginner level.
nuance: Stronger than 'basic': only the first, undeveloped stage, often a little crude.
personal: What skill do you have only a rudimentary grasp of, but would like to improve?
Who do you know who built something impressive with rudimentary tools?
hook: 'RUDE-imentary': a rude caveman with only the basics, a stick and a grunt.

intents: share one understanding of the plan, so nobody works from different ideas
when you check that you and your partner both mean the cheap hotel before you book
both clear about what was agreed, so there are no mix-ups later
ru_cue: одинаково понимать план и договоренности

upgrades.plain: Before we start, let's make sure we [all understand the plan the same way].
upgrades.better: Before we start, let's make sure we're all *on the same page*.

upgrades.plain: My husband and I [were working from two different plans] for the budget, and the wedding planner got caught in the middle.
upgrades.better: My husband and I weren't *on the same page* about the budget, and the wedding planner got caught in the middle.

upgrades.plain: A quick call [made sure we all understood the plan the same way] before the meeting.
upgrades.better: A quick call got us all *on the same page* before the meeting.

collocations.chunk: make sure we're on the same page
get everyone on the same page
not on the same page about

nuance: About sharing one understanding of a plan or the facts; see eye to eye is about agreeing in opinion.
personal: When did a mix-up happen because you weren't on the same page with someone?
Who are you usually on the same page with without even talking?
hook: Picture two people reading one book, both fingers on the very same line.

intents: very hard and tiring, needing effort over a long time
a long climb or journey where you keep having to stop and rest
a task that drains your strength, like restoring an old boat over a whole winter
ru_cue: очень тяжелый и долгий, требующий сил до самого конца

upgrades.plain: The climb was [really hard], and we had to stop three times on the way up.
upgrades.better: The climb was *arduous*, and we had to stop three times on the way up.

upgrades.plain: It was a [long, exhausting] journey across the moor in the rain.
upgrades.better: It was an *arduous* journey across the moor in the rain.

upgrades.plain: After an [exhausting] year of night classes, I finally got my degree, and my mum cried.
upgrades.better: After an *arduous* year of night classes, I finally got my degree, and my mum cried.

nuance: Hard because it takes long, tiring effort; tedious is boring, daunting is scary before you start.
personal: What was the most arduous journey you've ever made?
Who do you know who went through an arduous process to get where they are?
gesture: Trudge on the spot, leaning forward, and wipe your forehead.
hook: 'ARD-uous' sounds like 'hard-uous', or Russian 'ад' (hell): a long climb through hell.

intents: pointless, because it has no chance of working whatever you do
when you keep arguing with someone who never changes their mind
like chasing a bus that has already turned the corner
ru_cue: все равно ничего не выйдет, зря стараться

upgrades.plain: Arguing with him is [pointless]; he never changes his mind.
upgrades.better: Arguing with him is *futile*; he never changes his mind.

upgrades.plain: We searched for her ring for three days, but it was [no use]. She was heartbroken.
upgrades.better: We searched for her ring for three days, but it was *futile*. She was heartbroken.

upgrades.plain: It's [a waste of time] watering the garden in full sun.
upgrades.better: It's *futile* to water the garden in full sun.

nuance: Pointless because success is impossible; something merely boring or unimportant isn't futile.
personal: What is something you once tried that turned out to be completely futile?
Who in your family keeps making futile attempts to change someone else?
hook: 'FEW-tile': trying to hold back a flood with a few tiles. Pointless.
